findings.title: The functional `own-transfer` journey (motion reduced) fails 2-10% of runs on the branch and 0 of 100 on main: third run in a row
findings.detail: Run 1 saw 2 of 48, run 2 saw 3 of 40 and called it fixed by the 58/34 px size guesses. Run 3: the full `pnpm e2e` failed it once (`covered`: the Payments row `Public Bank → Ryt Bank` 390×58 sits under the sticky day header `Wed, 1 Jul`), and a dedicated repeat failed 2/40, 2/60, 6/60 (head) against 0/40 and 0/60 (main). I bisected by reverting one thing at a time: ripple off (`installPress()` commented out) 2/60; payments.tsx back to main's 40/56 guesses 8/60 (so run 2's sizes help but do not cure it); kit.tsx (skeleton fade) reverted 6/60; app-shell.tsx (`screen-region` wrapper) reverted 3/60. None cured it. The cause is unfound (a guess: another B05 change moves the Payments list's first frame; untested). The brief's Done-when says the functional suite must be reliable.

findings.title: Tests have no teeth for D140's own numbers and the long-press haptic: 6 of 7 probes survive the repo's suites
findings.detail: Probes, each made alone against `pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/{frame,lib,components}` and `e2e/motion.spec.ts --project preview` (the `feel` and `motion` suites). Survivors: `--motion-ms` 200 ms to 2000 ms; forward's new screen sliding in from the left (`sen-in-left`); the long-press haptic call deleted (`lib/long-press.ts`); the ripple's disabled-control guard removed; the shared-amount id check removed. Only the toggle-kind swap was caught. Run 2's QA specs (`qa/e2e/b05feel2-motion.spec.ts`) do kill the duration and direction probes (verified on probe builds), so they are held by QA specs but no mutant points at them, and nothing at all holds the long-press haptic: with it deleted, run 1 and 2's haptics and feel specs still pass 13 of 13.

findings.title: The feel pass (motion on, 4x CPU) still fails `scan-after` and `subscription` on the branch (2 of 42); main passes
findings.detail: Third run watching this. `Reading receipt…` is in the DOM for about 900 ms on 4 of 6 branch runs, 400 ms on 2 of 6, and 1000 ms on all 6 of main, so Playwright's polling misses it. `/s/reading` appears at about 80 ms and the text at about 450 ms; confirm replaces it at about 855 ms or 1340 ms on the branch (bimodal), 1430-1570 ms on main. Why the branch's reader finishes early in some runs is not explained. A person sees the Reading screen for a shorter time with a made-up reader only; a real reader takes seconds.

findings.title: 11 metrics flags; the taps that open a sheet or push a screen answer 60-150 ms later than main at 4x CPU
findings.detail: Flags: settings/categories blocking 639 vs 420; hawker/1 first change 312 vs 176; own-transfer/2 settle 709 vs 442; payday/5 735 vs 394; proposal/3 1228 vs 555; ask/2 208 vs 88; ask/3 settle 2246 vs 212; ask/4 336 vs 112; capture-off/4 328 vs 184; export/2 230 vs 116; members/11 532 vs 254. Measured causes: (a) the ripple costs 2-3 ms in its handler and the next frame comes within 22 ms at 4x on Review, Payments and Home (so a press IS answered in a frame; the film strips show it late because the video capture slows the page); (b) opening the category sheet from a Review chip takes pointerdown-to-sheet 237-269 ms with motion on, 344 ms with motion reduced, 180 ms on main: the extra is not the view transition; a CPU profile shows 138 ms of `getBoundingClientRect` self time on the branch (43 ms in `useSheetResize`'s first measure, 52 ms in vaul) and none on main, but removing the first measure left the median at 277 ms, so the cause is not found (a guess: layout moved earlier, not removed); (c) ask/3's 2246 ms is a metric artifact: Home to Insights tab to content is 2.07-2.46 s on the branch and 1.84-2.10 s on main (about +250 ms), Insights being slow on both. Verdict: pushes and tabs, accepted as run 1/2 did (the owner judges on the phone); sheet open +60-150 ms is unexplained and left open.

findings.title: Eyes pass: 6 `wrong` verdicts, weighed against main (none is a regression of the branch beyond the latency in finding 4)
findings.detail: hawker/2 and fix/5 (a closing sheet shows another step's title, 'Category'; the page changes late): measured the same on main (title flips to 'Category' at 560 ms on main, 663 on branch; row gone 560 vs 663 ms; toast 647 vs 790). own-transfer/1 (nothing for a second): the made-up write lands about 0.6-0.8 s after the tap at 4x on both; only the ripple answers earlier. ask/3: see finding 4c, a metric artifact. members/10 and the toast over sheets: the shared toast overlaps an open sheet by 58 px on main too (Ask Sen sheet: no control covered, chips partly). Pre-existing, so not B05's, but the destructive Remove confirm is the worst place for it. fix/4 (snap with a white void): run 2's sheet spec passes (settles under 450 ms) so the easing works; the one-frame void I could not reproduce at 1x. Undo's late effect (proposal/3, fix/6): Undo measured at 4x: toast gone and value back together at 525 ms (branch) and 550 ms (main).

findings.title: A scroll that starts on a row flashes a ripple
findings.detail: The ripple starts on pointerdown by design, so a drag that begins on a list row shows one (faint, 12% opacity) before the browser decides it is a scroll. Measured: one ripple created by one scroll gesture over Payments, gone within about 400 ms. Android's own ripple waits about 100 ms for this reason. Left to the owner's phone.

findings.title: Fixed since run 2, verified
findings.detail: Run 2's 1 (sheet creeping): the category-sheet settle spec passes. 2 (Home tab to More): `Home` flake spec passes 40 of 40. 3 (Payments row guess): sizes now 34/58, but see finding 1. 6 (label rows): a real press on a label row's text now shows a ripple (the run-2 spec aimed at the checkbox's own indicator and failed; I corrected its target). 7: `field.test.tsx` pins reject. Five of run 2's six `motion` mutants and all 25 in `qa/mutants.ts` are killed (25/25).

findings.title: Small notes
findings.detail: Payments scroll resets to the top on back, on main too (not a regression). A browser's long-press still calls `navigator.vibrate(10)`, where patterns §8 says a browser has none (pre-existing from B03). Run 1's measurement specs (`b05feel-newlook`, `-tabsettle`, `-vtlen`) assume main on another port and fail without it. Kotlin's `hapticConstant` mapping and `ShellTest` need an emulator; not run. `threshold` has no user.
